appropriate: a slab L standing on a heavy rule reads as a ledger's ruled line or bottom line and fits the plain Everyman/Sage tone, but 'see where you stand' needs a sentence to arrive
distinctive: no circle badge, cyan or rounded lowercase like the category, but a serif initial over an underline is a generic silhouette; the icon is a letter in a green tile
simple: one slab L and one bar beneath it; drawable from memory in two strokes
legible: 'Clear Ledger' reads cleanly in the header, dark nav and card; the L holds at 16 px, though the gap between L and rule is tight there
adaptable: black, reversed, one-colour 64/32, the app tile, browser tab and avatar all hold; no hairlines, so the receipt printer should cope; the rule gives an obvious draw-in motion
timeless: a bracketed slab serif and a rule, no trend shape; the mono-initial icon is a use-carefully item that strategy section 8 justifies
universal: the mirrored panel reads as a J on a bar and the rotated panel as a bracket; both are just the mark turned, no unintended image
clear: unsearched: underlined serif initials are common across law, publishing and accountancy practices; nothing I know copies this exact L-on-rule in sole-trader bookkeeping
congruent: deep ink green, static, grounded flat base, lightly framed by a rule, sturdy text serif all match; the L is asymmetric against the 0.8 symmetry target and heavier than medium
system: horizontal lockups, the 256-to-16 ladder, the app icon, favicon tab, avatar and card are drawn; no stacked lockup on the sheet and the icon is an L, not the CL pairing the strategy proposed
